§ 01

Overview

The IEEE Signal Processing Society Malaysia Chapter and Universiti Tunku Abdul Rahman jointly organise the 14ᵗʰ Symposium on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing on 10 August 2026 — a free, in-person gathering open to students, academics, industry professionals and IEEE / non-IEEE members alike.

Objectives
  • Bring the university and industry together to share and discuss the latest trends in signal processing.
  • Serve as a forum for knowledge sharing on signal processing technology and for professional networking.

§ 03

Keynote Speakers

Assoc. Prof. Ir. Dr. Lim Einly
Department of Biomedical Engineering, Universiti Malaya, Malaysia · Founder, Asian Cardiac Engineering Laboratory
Keynote Title
“Beyond Data: Integrating Signal Processing and Mechanistic Modeling for Personalized Cardiovascular Medicine”
Abstract

Advances in signal processing and artificial intelligence have enabled the extraction of increasingly sophisticated information from physiological signals and medical images. Yet, many clinical decisions continue to rely on descriptive biomarkers and statistical associations that provide limited insight into the mechanisms underlying cardiovascular disease. As healthcare moves toward personalization, there is a growing need to complement data-driven approaches with mechanistic understanding.

This keynote presents a research journey that bridges biomedical signal processing, medical imaging, and cardiovascular modeling to investigate how physiological measurements can be transformed into mechanistic knowledge. Through examples involving autonomic function assessment, cardiovascular magnetic resonance imaging, ventricular-arterial coupling, and patient-specific computational modeling, the talk will illustrate how signals and images can be translated into quantitative representations of cardiovascular structure, function, and adaptation. Particular emphasis will be placed on the role of mechanistic models in explaining observations that cannot be fully understood from data alone.

The integration of multimodal physiological measurements, artificial intelligence, and physics-based cardiovascular models offers a pathway toward digital twins and personalized cardiovascular medicine. By combining the strengths of signal processing and mechanistic modeling, future healthcare systems may progress from simply measuring disease to understanding, predicting, and ultimately preventing it.

Biography

Assoc. Prof. Ir. Dr. Lim Einly is an Associate Professor in the Department of Biomedical Engineering at Universiti Malaya and the founder of the Asian Cardiac Engineering Laboratory. Her research is deeply embedded at the engineering–medicine interface, focusing on biomedical signal processing, medical image analysis, personalized cardiovascular modeling, and telehealth technologies. Aligning with the core themes of SASSP 2026, Dr. Lim's work bridges data-driven signal processing with physics-based mechanistic models to transform multimodal cardiovascular data into clinically meaningful insights. She integrates biomedical signal processing, medical imaging, machine learning, and advanced computational modeling techniques—including Computational Fluid Dynamics (CFD) and Fluid-Structure Interaction (FSI)—to investigate disease mechanisms and support personalized treatment strategies for complex cardiovascular conditions such as aortic dissection, valvular disease, hypertension, and myocardial infarction.

Dr. Lim is a Chartered Engineer (UK) and Professional Engineer (Malaysia). She has authored more than 70 Web of Science-indexed journal publications and secured over RM3 million in competitive research funding, including the prestigious Royal Society (UK) Newton Advanced Fellowship. She currently serves as Vice President of the Asia-Pacific Society for Artificial Organs (APSAO) and was awarded the APSAO Chairpersonship Award in 2023. Research Group Website: https://www.asiancardiac.org

Prof. Teddy Surya Gunawan
Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering, International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM)
Keynote Title
“From Signals to Intelligence: Attention-Driven Deep Learning for Signal, Image, and Atmospheric Sensing”
Abstract

The past decade has witnessed a profound transformation in how we process and interpret signals, not merely through smarter algorithms, but through architectures that learn where to look. This keynote traces a research journey across three connected frontiers: biomedical signal and image analysis, aerial object detection, and physics-guided deep learning for atmospheric optical sensing.

The talk opens by examining how attention mechanisms, particularly Convolutional Block Attention Modules (CBAM) and dual-branch fusion architectures, have elevated the detection and classification of clinically significant conditions from medical imaging data, including spinal disorder classification from X-rays. The speaker demonstrates how thoughtful architectural design, stratified evaluation, and class-imbalance handling produce models that are not just accurate but also deployable and trustworthy in clinical settings.

The second segment addresses edge-based signal intelligence, drawing on published work on small-drone detection using optimized YOLOv8 with attention mechanisms and on instrumentation-driven approaches for remote sensing. These cases illustrate how integrating domain knowledge into neural architecture design yields measurable gains in detection performance under real-world constraints.

The talk concludes by extending these principles into an active research frontier: the Adaptive Physics-Guided Transformer (APGT), an AOARD-funded project targeting image restoration from atmospheric turbulence degradation. Here, Kolmogorov turbulence statistics, Zernike wavefront priors, and explainable AI are embedded directly into transformer attention, bridging the gap between physical understanding and data-driven learning. The session closes with a reflection on a unifying principle: in signal processing and AI alike, knowing where to look, analytically, patiently, and precisely, remains the essential discipline.

Biography

Teddy Surya Gunawan (Senior Member, IEEE) is a Professor in the Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering at the International Islamic University Malaysia (IIUM). He obtained his B.Eng. with cum laude honors in Electrical Engineering from Institut Teknologi Bandung (ITB), Indonesia, in 1998; his M.Eng. from Nanyang Technological University, Singapore, in 2001; and his Ph.D. from the University of New South Wales (UNSW), Australia, in 2007. Prof. Gunawan has held esteemed roles, including Visiting Research Fellow at UNSW (2010–2021) and Adjunct Professor at Telkom University (2022–2023), and he has been a Senior Member of IEEE since 2012, previously chairing the IEEE Instrumentation and Measurement Society – Malaysia Section.

Recognized for his contributions to speech and audio processing, biomedical signal processing, image and video processing, and parallel computing, he received IIUM's Best Researcher Award in 2018 and is listed among the World's Top 2% Scientists in Artificial Intelligence and Image Processing by Elsevier for 2023 and 2024. He holds multiple professional engineering certifications, including Fellow Member and Chartered Professional Engineer (CPEng) of Engineers Australia; Insinyur Profesional Utama (PII, Indonesia); ASEAN Engineer; ASEAN Chartered Professional Engineer; and APEC Engineer. Within IIUM, he has also served as Head of Department (2015–2016) and Head of Programme Accreditation and Quality Assurance (2017–2018) at the Faculty of Engineering.

Mr. Ali MuzaffarOnline
Senior Manager, Product Privacy and AI Governance, Meta Platforms, USA · IEEE Senior Member
Keynote Title
“From Algorithms to Accountability: AI Governance in Practice and How to Build a Career in It”
Abstract

As generative AI systems move from research labs into products touching billions of users, the need for robust governance has never been more urgent — nor the career opportunity more wide open. This keynote bridges two worlds: the practitioner's reality of governing AI at scale, and the student's question of how to get there.

The first half draws on experience overseeing 70+ GenAI product launches and 80+ LLM development programs at one of the world's largest technology platforms, presenting a real-world framework for responsible AI deployment — covering privacy-by-design, risk-tiered review architectures, cross-functional accountability, and incident response. Attendees will gain a grounded view of how AI governance actually operates inside a major technology company, and where the field must evolve next.

The second half speaks directly to students and early-career professionals: what skills matter most in AI governance (technical fluency, policy literacy, systems thinking, ethical reasoning), which certifications and IEEE pathways accelerate entry, and how the discipline bridges signal processing, data science, law, and ethics — making it uniquely suited to engineers who want impact beyond the algorithm.

Whether you are building models or building careers, the future belongs to those who can make AI trustworthy at scale.

Biography

Ali Muzaffar's journey began in India, where a passion for electronics set him on a path spanning three continents. His first stop was Malaysia, where he worked as a Research Assistant at Multimedia University (MMU) — an experience that deepened his technical foundation and forged a lasting connection to Southeast Asia's engineering community.

From there, Ali pursued graduate studies at the University of California, Irvine, before launching a career at the intersection of technology, trust, and governance. At Deloitte, he led Trustworthy AI and GRC programs for Fortune 50 clients across financial services, healthcare, and the public sector. He then joined Meta Platforms as Senior Manager of Product Privacy and AI Governance, shaping how one of the world's most influential technology companies deploys AI responsibly — leading governance programs across 70+ generative AI launches, including Llama 2 through 4 with over 1.2 billion downloads globally, and establishing privacy frameworks used by more than 40,000 engineers worldwide. His professional work on privacy at scale has been recognized in publications including Science and Nature.

Beyond industry, Ali is an IEEE Senior Member with over 14 years of volunteer leadership — serving as a Board Member of IEEE SSIT, a leader within IEEE's Education Activities Division, and a frequent speaker and mentor across IEEE communities globally. He is currently working on IEEE RAISE (Responsible AI for Students and Educators), a K-12 initiative bringing responsible AI education to students across five countries.

Ali's story — from India to Kuala Lumpur to Silicon Valley — is a testament to what engineers can achieve when technical excellence meets ethical responsibility.

Prof. Chen ChenOnline
Xidian University, Xi'an, China (Professor & Ph.D. Advisor) · Director, Xi'an Key Laboratory of Mobile Edge Computing and Security
Keynote Title
“Intelligent Driving: Research and Practice”
Abstract

Intelligent driving has become a key technology for modern automotive and transportation development. However, it still suffers from unstable perception, poor decision interpretability, insufficient planning robustness and limited control adaptability in complex traffic scenarios. This talk systematically explores the core theories of intelligent driving covering perception, decision-making, planning and control, and presents our corresponding engineering practices. Through algorithm optimization, simulation and real-vehicle verification, combined with industry-university cooperation, the research improves system robustness and functional safety. This work provides valuable references for the industrial advancement of intelligent driving technologies.

Biography

Prof. Chen Chen is a Professor, Ph.D. Advisor, and Doctor of Engineering at Xidian University, China. He has been selected as a High-Level Talent of Shaanxi Province, a High-Level Talent of Xi'an City, and a Qinchuangyuan Innovation Talent. He currently serves as Director of the Xi'an Key Laboratory of Mobile Edge Computing and Security and as Discipline Leader in Intelligent Transportation Internet of Things at Xidian University, alongside leadership roles spanning the Xidian China–Malaysia Science and Technology Institute, the Automotive Electronics Research Institute of Xidian University Hangzhou Research Institute, and joint laboratories with Geely, Lotus, and Molead on intelligent connected vehicles. He is a Distinguished Member of the China Computer Federation (CCF), a Senior Member of IEEE and of the China Institute of Communications, and a member of ACM and the Chinese Institute of Electronics.

His research focuses on mobile edge computing, the Internet of Vehicles, intelligent transportation, intelligent connected vehicles, vehicular communication, and communication security. Appointed a Master's Supervisor in 2010 and a Ph.D. Supervisor in 2016, he has undertaken research visits at Oak Ridge National Laboratory and the University of California, Santa Barbara. He has led numerous national and provincial research projects — including key and general programs of the National Natural Science Foundation of China — and industry collaborations with partners such as Huawei, State Grid, and CETC. He has published more than 140 papers in leading journals and conferences (including IEEE COMST, IoT-J, TMC, TVT, and TITS), with 24 ESI Highly Cited Papers and two authored monographs, and has been named among the World's Top 2% Scientists and Elsevier's China Highly Cited Scholars (2025–2026).
